lines.text: The Teacher says all labor and success spring from a man's envy of his neighbor, and better is one handful with tranquility.
The Teacher sees a man all alone, without even a son or brother, whose eyes are never content with his wealth.
Two are better than one because they have a good return, and if one falls, his companion can lift him up.
If two lie down together they keep warm, and a cord of five strands is not quickly broken.
A poor but wise youth is better than an old foolish king, and the youth came from the palace to the kingship.
